145478885.title: File:Memorial Plaque for Walter Wilsdorff, Neuschwanstein Castle Administrator.jpg

ObjectName.value: Memorial Plaque for Walter Wilsdorff, Neuschwanstein Castle Administrator

Categories.value: Crucifixes in Germany|CC-Zero|Commemorative plaques|Self-published work|Neuschwanstein Castle|Media created with Nikon Z7ii provided by the Quebec WikiClub|Images from Munich Project|Fortifications by Wilfredor

ImageDescription.value: This roadside crucifix and memorial plaque commemorate Walter Wilsdorff (4 February 1905 – 29 October 1953), the administrator of Neuschwanstein Castle. The German inscription states that he “died in an accident while on duty.” Contemporary references to the incident indicate that Wilsdorff was fatally injured during forestry work near Neuschwanstein in 1953, reportedly after being struck by a tree. The memorial, placed on the lower road leading toward the castle, marks the death of a castle official whose work was tied not only to the building itself but also to the surrounding estate and landscape. The crucifix reflects the local Bavarian Catholic tradition of roadside memorials for people who died suddenly or tragically.
